title: How one dances before the kallah
summary: The gittin Dovid's soldiers gave before going to war, the blessing "go take what you have acquired," and why a widow is called almanah. What the mizbeach does for Klal Yisrael, when to eat dates, and the three things no person escapes each day. Then the famous question of how one dances before the kallah, the dancing that brought the Shechinah, the song when the Rabbanan gave semicha, and the radiance of a face.

key_ideas: Dovid's soldiers gave gittin before going to war so they could fight fully focused, as the Kotzker Rebbe explains.
Three things no one escapes each day: thoughts of sin, iyun tefillah, and the dust of lashon hara.
Davening as a child asks a parent, not as one who deserves, keeps a person from bringing judgment on himself.
How one dances before the kallah: Beis Hillel praise every kallah as beautiful and gracious.
